findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name: "shards" vs "shard"
findings.body: In `SpanFlusher.main`, the `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` timer uses tag key `"shard"` (line 185) while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses tag key `"shards"` (line 199). This inconsistency will make it difficult to query or correlate these metrics in dashboards and alerts, as they use different tag names for the same dimension.

findings.title: join() passes full timeout to next_step, leaving no time for process cleanup
findings.body: In `join()`, `self.next_step.join(timeout)` is called with the full timeout value. The deadline is computed before this call, but if `next_step.join` consumes the entire timeout, the subsequent loop over processes will immediately break (remaining_time <= 0) without calling `process.terminate()` on any of them. With multiple processes this is more likely to be an issue than with the previous single-process design. The timeout should be split or `next_step.join` should be given a portion of the total timeout.

findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op due to monkeypatch, making test potentially flaky
findings.body: The test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to a no-op on line 15 (`monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`), then calls `time.sleep(0.1)` on line 62 with the comment 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change'. Since `time.sleep` is globally patched, this call does nothing and does not actually give the flusher threads any real time. The test currently passes because the flusher's own `time.sleep(1)` is also patched (making it spin fast), but this makes the test fragile and the comment misleading. If the flusher logic changes to not spin, this test could become flaky.

findings.title: _create_process_for_shard is dead code
findings.body: The method `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is defined at line 127 but is never called anywhere in the codebase. It appears to be leftover from an earlier design iteration where individual shards could be restarted independently. This dead code adds confusion about the intended restart semantics.

findings.title: Backpressure from any single process blocks all shards
findings.body: In `submit()`, if ANY process's `backpressure_since` exceeds the threshold, `MessageRejected` is raised, blocking insertion for ALL shards. With multiple processes each handling different shards, a single slow shard now blocks progress for all other shards. In the previous single-process design this was unavoidable, but with the multiprocess design, healthy processes could continue flushing their shards while one is under pressure. This could cause cascading backpressure and reduce the benefit of parallelism.
